messages:
anya: Heads-up — customer Graybox reported p99 spikes on embeddings in eu-west last hour, SLO breach. Seen similar alerts in our monitoring. Anyone oncall who can triage? :frowning:
marie: Which cluster/shard and what time window? any repro steps from support or request ids?
anya: eu-west-2, shard g10-2. Customer run id 8923, spikes around 23:10-23:30 UTC. Traces show long tail on token streaming calls and a bunch of KV cache misses. Link to traces: https://redwood/trace/8923 :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy finished: nvdriver-536.2, kernel-6.2.8 @ 2026-03-16T23:12:47Z
samir: We rolled nvdriver 535.10 -> 536.2 last night on the eu-west pool as part of the CUDA14 prep. Also kernel bumped on a subset of nodes (6.1 -> 6.2) at the same window.
oz: I pulled metrics — NVMe io_wait spiking and queue_depth hitting caps on nvme0n1 for the affected hosts. KV cache fetch latency correlated with the qdepth spikes (many small reads). iostat snapshot:
```
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  %util
nvme0n1      3200.00  40.00  51200  1024   24.5  98.5
```
oz: Suggests IO scheduling/backpressure from driver+kernel combo. Also seeing higher scheduler latencies in kernel logs.
marie: Can we confirm whether it's nvme scheduler change or driver NVMe offloads? samir, any known changes in nvme defaults with 536.2? 
samir: 536.2 introduced a deferred-descriptor path for tiny IOs that changed submission patterns. We didn't expect queue_depth pressure, but combined with kernel 6.2 blk-mq changes it can surface. No customer-facing issues reported until now.
anya: Customer is asking for ETA — they want either rollback or mitigation. Their traffic is production critical.
marie: Immediate mitigations we can try (ordered):
- Canary rollback driver on 4 nodes (requires reboot) — quickest to validate impact.
- Tune per-block q depth: echo 128 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests on canary nodes.
- Temporarily reduce model batch size / concurrency for embeddings route at the routing layer to lower IO rate.
- Enable more aggressive KV cache warmup + local cache to reduce misses.
samir: Note: rollback needs coordination with capacity; I can cordon two nodes and restart pods elsewhere. Rolling all will take ~30-45m plus rebalancing.
oz: I can push a non-reboot tunable for an experiment to lower nr_requests and also drop writeback aggressiveness. Example commands:
```
echo 128 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests
sysctl -w vm.dirty_ratio=5
```
oz: Also recommend throttling request concurrency at the routing layer for embeddings: set route concurrency=8 from 16 for eu-west-embeds for next 15m.
marie: Action owners: samir = rollback / cordon, oz = kernel tunables + route throttles, anya = customer comms and get their traffic window, marie = monitoring and rollback decision.
kevin: Thanks, any ETA? Graybox needs target ETA for business team. If rollback will be disruptive, prefer config tweaks first.
samir: Starting canary rollback on 2 nodes now, will report p95/p99 after they come up. If canary looks good, we'll continue in batches.
marie: Update in 12m: canary nodes back up with driver 535.10, no kernel change. Initial metrics: embeddings p95 dropped from ~420ms -> ~110ms, p99 down ~70%. Storage qdepth on those nodes normalized.
anya: Passing this to Graybox — they asked to keep rolling until their SLOs stable. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
marie: Proceeding with staged rollback; will post progress. If rollback shows regressions elsewhere, we'll pause and revert to the tunables plan.
